sermon.title: The Supernatural Display of the Power of God from the Beginning of the Gospel 02/11/2018
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: Pastor David G. Kincer shows that the gospel began supernaturally—the Word made flesh, an angel, God’s glory, a manger sign, a heavenly host and a guiding star—and will end supernaturally with angels gathering the elect. Since it is supernatural at both ends, it is reasonable that God still works supernaturally now. Every visitation must be tested by its message.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: Garbled names marked [unclear] (a Jesus-only healing evangelist of the late 1940s, “William [unclear]”). Kept as spoken: “seven pillars” of Islam (47:00); “Thessalonians 1 verses 4 through 13 I mean chapter 4 verse 13.” Points to check: Obama said the Bible approves slavery and he wrote to him (6:40); no angel in scripture has wings. Sensitive content kept as spoken: liberal churches “lying” about the virgin birth; life begins at conception; Allah, the Hindu god; Mormons, Muslims, Jehovah’s Witnesses, Seventh-day Adventists, Buddhists and Hindus from angels “with a wrong message”; Todd Bentley, the Lakeland revival, the angel “Emma” and the Kansas City prophets called “nincompoops,” gold dust and glitter (31:40–37:30); a demon suffocating him; public schools teaching Islam.

scriptures.text_nkjv: But I do not want you to be ignorant, brethren, concerning those who have fallen asleep, lest you sorrow as others who have no hope. For if we believe that Jesus died and rose again, even so God will bring with Him those who sleep in Jesus. For this we say to you by the word of the Lord, that we who are alive and remain until the coming of the Lord will by no means precede those who are asleep. For the Lord Himself will descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of an archangel, and with the trumpet of God. And the dead in Christ will rise first. Then we who are alive and remain shall be caught up together with them in the clouds to meet the Lord in the air. And thus we shall always be with the Lord. Therefore comfort one another with these words.

Repent therefore and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out, so that times of refreshing may come from the presence of the Lord, and that He may send Jesus Christ, who was preached to you before, whom heaven must receive until the times of restoration of all things, which God has spoken by the mouth of all His holy prophets since the world began.
